clue.text: On the way back, friends sprint in a careless manner

indicators.note: travelling back means the word for friends is read from its end to its start

parts.note: pals are friends
a dash is a sprint

explanation.surface: Heading home, a group of mates run off without much care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the way back' reverses the word for friends; 'sprint' reads as a verb in the surface but supplies a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is done hastily and carelessly, so the adverb fits a careless manner.

clue.text: Extremely easy task for the broody type

definitions.meaning: a simple catch or chance that should not be missed, in sporting slang
a hen that sits on her eggs to hatch them

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word between the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolly catch in cricket or an open goal is called this; a broody hen settles on eggs.

clue.text: Drivers taking tank in last part of war movie

indicators.note: the drivers' body takes the tank into itself, enclosing it

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation for drivers
a vat is a large tank for liquid

indicators.note: the final letter of the word war is used

explanation.surface: Motorists commandeer a tank in the closing stage of a war film.
explanation.definitionFit: Avatar is James Cameron's 2009 science-fiction film, here an example of a film title.

clue.text: Mysteriously, is around no longer

indicators.note: something done mysteriously happens in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something strangely is not here any more.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of IS AROUND, signalled by 'Mysteriously', gives the answer; the whole clue describes an extinct creature.
explanation.definitionFit: These prehistoric reptiles died out long ago, so they are creatures not present any more.

clue.text: Fat girl on diet, finally

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

indicators.note: the closing letter of the word diet is taken

explanation.surface: An overweight young woman goes on a diet at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like an adjective describing the girl but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet is the hard animal fat used in British puddings and pastry.

clue.text: Plunder special paints

parts.note: special gives SP
oils are oil paints, as in a painting done in oils

explanation.surface: Looters make off with a set of special artist's paints.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoils are goods taken in war or robbery, which is what plunder means as a noun.

clue.text: What, ultimately, is added to tree to make it grow? Earth, perhaps

indicators.note: the closing letter is placed after the tree name, joined on at its end

parts.note: the plane is a tree common in London streets

indicators.note: the final letter of the word What is taken

explanation.surface: A gardening question about what to add to a tree to make it grow, answered with soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Earth' looks like garden soil answering the question, but it is the world we live on.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is one of the worlds orbiting the Sun, an example of that class of body.

clue.text: Secured hat — being eccentric

indicators.note: being eccentric means behaving oddly, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An odd person has got hold of a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of HAT BEING, signalled by 'eccentric', gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as good as won or certain is said to be already pocketed and assured.

clue.text: Cocktail salesmen hang around outside posh hotel for

indicators.note: the salesmen's letters go outside the hotel name, enclosing it
turning around means the word for salesmen is reversed

parts.note: reps are sales representatives
the Ritz is a famously luxurious London hotel

explanation.surface: Sales staff loiter outside a smart hotel waiting for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hang around' reverses the salesmen, giving SPER, which wraps the hotel; the trailing 'for' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spritzer is a mixed drink of white wine and soda water.

clue.text: What every man is said to want in the school place

definitions.text: What every man is said to want

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
to place something is to set it down

explanation.surface: A remark about what all men supposedly desire, located somewhere on school premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' and 'place' look like nouns but are both verbs here; 'in the' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A model railway layout is the proverbial toy every man secretly longs for, a cliche about grown men.

clue.text: Bird of prey terrified parrot

indicators.note: a terrified creature is thrown into disorder, so the letters of parrot are scrambled

explanation.surface: A hawk has frightened a parrot out of its wits.
explanation.definitionFit: A raptor is the general term for a hunting bird such as an eagle, hawk or falcon.

clue.text: Duck comes from the row of shops on a road

parts.note: a mall is a shopping precinct

explanation.surface: A duck emerges from the shopping parade onto the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck, the drake with a green head.

clue.text: If it looks different, please go by

indicators.note: if the word please looks different its letters have been rearranged

explanation.surface: A polite request that time pass if things appear changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If it' is linking padding; 'looks different' rearranges PLEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that elapses passes or slips away, the sense of going by.

clue.text: Adhesive put round a second window frame

indicators.note: the adhesive is placed around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: cement is a binding adhesive

explanation.surface: Someone uses glue around a frame to fix a second window in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A casement is a hinged window sash, the frame that swings open on its side.

clue.text: Wanted one way to address a man during act

indicators.note: the form of address is placed in the middle of the act, falling within it

parts.note: a deed is an act

parts.words: one way to address a man
parts.note: sir is a polite way to address a man

explanation.surface: A man is spoken to formally in the middle of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something desired is longed for, so it was wanted.

clue.text: Copper left in genuine panacea

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the letter for left goes within the word for genuine

parts.note: real means genuine

explanation.surface: A copper bracelet left in place as a true cure for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A panacea is a supposed remedy for every ill, which is exactly what a universal cure claims to be.

clue.text: Produced cheese on return

indicators.note: returning sends the cheese name back the way it came, so it is read backwards

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

explanation.surface: Cheese was made available when brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: To have made something is to have produced it, both past forms of creating.

clue.text: Being cut left a doctor and policeman outside hospital

parts.note: MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

indicators.note: the policeman's letters sit outside the hospital letter, around it

parts.note: a cop is a policeman

explanation.surface: Someone injured was left by a medic and an officer outside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a link word; 'cut' suggests a wound, but it is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop from a young sheep is a cut of meat, a portion of the carcass.

clue.text: Expression of annoyance with a precious item upset Madonna, say

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset item is turned upside down, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: rats is an exclamation of irritation
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: Irritated about a precious possession, the pop singer gets cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RATS + A + GEM into the answer; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Madonna is a pop star of the greatest fame, an example of a superstar.

clue.text: Cut estimate after fabric is seen

indicators.note: the estimate comes after the fabric, placed behind it

parts.note: lace is a delicate fabric
to rate is to estimate or assess

explanation.surface: Someone trims a quote once they have seen the material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is seen' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or gash flesh, a violent form of wounding.

clue.text: Assist with a back

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it

explanation.surface: Help someone by supporting them from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word; 'back' is the verb used of a wager, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, usually in wrongdoing, so it means assist.

clue.text: Watch words!

parts.note: read literally as an instruction to look at spoken words rather than hear them, the skill of following speech by sight

explanation.definitionFit: Lip-readers understand speech by observing mouth movements, literally watching what is said.

clue.text: Place many go to is set out differently

definitions.meaning: a holiday destination visited by crowds
arranged again in a new order, sorted afresh

explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the two senses; the second reads the word as RE-SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside town is a holiday destination, and to re-sort things is to rearrange them.

clue.text: First platoon involved in attacks — they may be shot

indicators.note: the letter is caught up inside the attacks, placed within them

parts.note: raids are attacks

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word platoon is taken

explanation.surface: The leading platoon takes part in assaults where men may be shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' suggests gunfire in a military scene, but canoeists shoot rapids by riding through them.
explanation.definitionFit: White-water stretches are ridden through fast by canoes, which is what shooting them means.

clue.text: Refer to piece of publicity

definitions.meaning: an old verb meaning to mention or turn attention to something

explanation.surface: Mention a promotional item.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to a matter is to allude to it; also short for advertisement.

clue.text: Support church and allow jewellery

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
CE is the Church of England
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A church supports and permits the wearing of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a band or chain worn round the wrist as an ornament.

clue.text: Wage war when overdrawn?

indicators.note: the word for war sits within the state of being overdrawn, set inside its letters

parts.note: an overdrawn account is in the red

explanation.surface: Fighting a battle while one's bank account is in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wage' looks like a verb paired with war but is the noun definition; an overdrawn account is 'in the red', in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something paid in return for work or service, as wages are.

clue.text: Love to visit distant Portuguese, 22

parts.note: far means distant
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: Romance calls on a faraway Portuguese.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is RESORT, so the definition is a Portuguese resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is the Algarve town in southern Portugal, an example of a holiday destination.

clue.text: Food served at arena when seeing powerful boxer?

definitions.meaning: a sausage in a bun, sold at stadiums and sports venues
a boxer is a dog breed, and a hot one would be powerful, the question mark flagging the whimsy

explanation.surface: Stadium snacks on sale while watching a strong fighter in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a prizefighter at the arena, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A frankfurter in a roll is street food at games; a hot canine is jocularly a strong dog.

clue.text: American state with a pit producing zinc ore

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
a mine is a pit

explanation.surface: A US state where a mine yields zinc.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamine is a mineral source of zinc, also the pink lotion made from zinc compounds.

clue.text: I talk stupidly about silver, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for talking stupidly goes round the letter I, enclosing it

parts.note: to prate is to chatter foolishly

explanation.surface: Someone admits babbling nonsense on the subject of silver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silver' looks like the metal, but it is Long John Silver of Treasure Island, so the capital is hidden at the start of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the buccaneer of Stevenson's Treasure Island, an example of a seafaring robber.

clue.text: Maugham season broadcast on TV?

indicators.note: broadcast means the word for a season is spoken aloud, giving a spelling with the same sound

parts.note: summer is a season
a TV set

explanation.surface: Writer Maugham's season is aired on television.
explanation.walkthrough: W. Somerset Maugham was an English novelist; SOMERSET is also an English county, pronounced as if 'summer-set'.
explanation.definitionFit: The author W. Somerset Maugham used his middle name as his usual name, so the forename identifies the novelist.
